JeanBaptisteShow, que sa communauté appe: JeanBaptisteShow, simply called JB by his community, has been posting on YouTube since 2013. On internet time, that's Antiquity: when his first video came out, TikTok didn't exist, Twitch had just been born and "content creator" wasn't a job yet. Twelve years later, the channel has nearly a million subscribers, around 500 videos and over 165 million views — a bricklayer's numbers rather than a viral hit's, laid brick by brick. Alex describes him as respected by a whole generation of gaming video makers, from Joueur du Grenier to Hugo Terra.
Il touche à tout : tests, analyses, hist: He does a bit of everything: reviews, analyses, video game history, PC builds, Twitch streams and more personal videos. Two pillars stand out: "Jean Quête d'actu", the live weekly video game news debrief on Wednesdays at 6 p.m., also available as a podcast, and "La vérité" ("The Truth"), where he compares two big names and settles it — with the definite article. His subscribers are "the Jeans", and right at the bottom of his descriptions, where nobody reads, he slips in: "I wish you lots of love, young Jean." Everyone else? Infamous.
C'est sa signature : les vannes sont pos: It's his signature: the jokes land, the editing breathes, zero filler. You can feel someone who spent more time on the video than you'll spend watching it. In the age of disposable content, it's almost an act of resistance.
Chaque fin d'année, il montait un PC de: Every year-end, he used to build a complete gaming PC for 500 euros: the holy grail of the broke student, awaited like an Advent calendar. The tradition stopped when the market made the feat impossible. Today, 500 euros buys you some RAM — and only if you haggle.
Pour Alex, JB est le premier vrai YouTub: For Alex, JB is the first true French gaming YouTuber in the noble sense: he proved you could write about video games like literature. After him came those who added method and sources, from Game Next Door to Fin du Game — which, incidentally, had him on as a guest.
Alex l'assume d'entrée : il est fan, au: Alex says it up front: he's a fan, to the point of sending Lolo fourteen voice messages one Sunday. Today's assessment was out of 500 euros rather than 10 — 480 for writing, 500 for loyalty to the community, 490 for longevity, 12 for the ability to build a 500-euro PC in 2026 (and that's not his fault). But the highlight is elsewhere: JB regularly talks about himself, his anxieties and a perfectionism that stops him from releasing a video that's never good enough. Alex, who struggles with exactly the same flaw, says it plainly: there were times these videos kept him going. That, Lolo replied, is exactly why this podcast exists.
La seule réserve tient du compliment dég: The only reservation is a disguised compliment: we wish he posted more often. The pace is slow, the work is done almost alone, and collaborations never last very long. But in a landscape where channels born in 2013 were nearly all dead by 2016, the achievement isn't the peak: it's never leaving the stage. Where to start: any video about a game you've already played, to measure everything you'd missed; then a 500-euro PC to understand the character, a personal video to understand the man, and his appearance on Fin du Game to understand the lineage.
« Dans un internet qui consomme ses star: “In an internet that burns through its stars in eighteen months, lasting twelve years while staying yourself is almost a technical feat. Harder, even, than a 500-euro PC.”
